"https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5109", "title": "feat(gdn): add SM8x prefill for the gated delta rule, fused and chunk-parallel", "body": "<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->\n\n## \ud83d\udccc Description\n\nThe SM8x fused prefill kernel for the gated delta rule assigns one block to each `(sequence, head, value slice)`. This provides enough parallelism for larger batches, but underutilizes the GPU on a single long sequence: only a few blocks are resident, and each walks the whole token axis serially. For `1x8192` with two heads it reached 0.60x of the vendored flash-linear-attention Triton op.\n\nThis PR adds:\n\n1. a **chunk-parallel path** that splits the token axis across blocks and reconciles the per-chunk states afterwards;\n2. a **pointer ABI** and a shared invocation context, which reduce the host-side launch overhead that path incurs;\n3. a **`v32` specialization** of the fused kernel for one measured shape that neither path won.\n\nIt also adds the dispatch logic that selects between them, and tests that pin the selection.\n\n## Chunk-parallel path\n\nThe state recurrence is serial in the token axis. A chunk-parallel decomposition cannot remove that, only shorten the chain each block walks and repair the result afterwards. Four launches:\n\n| stage | what it computes |\n|---|---|\n| `T` precompute | the per-chunk inverse `(I + tril(diag(beta) K K^T, -1))^{-1}` |\n| `MN` precompute | each chunk's local state contribution and its output term |\n| `fixup` | the serial scan over chunks that turns local states into absolute ones |\n| prefill | the per-chunk output, reading the reconciled state |\n\nOnly `fixup` is serial, and it is serial over chunks rather than tokens: at a 2048-token chunk an 8192-token sequence scans four, where the fused kernel walks 128 block iterations. The other three stages are parallel over `(chunk, head)`.\n\n`CollectiveInverse` is shared with the fused kernel rather than forked, as it already is with the SM90 and SM120 paths.\n\n## Launch overhead\n\nA CP call launches four kernels. With the tensor ABI, repeated `from_dlpack` conversion and layout construction per tensor per launch accounted for most of the call. Two changes:\n\n**Pointer ABI.** Each stage has a variant taking `cute.runtime.make_ptr` pointers plus host-rebuilt layouts instead of DLPack tensors. Every entry is alignment-checked against the layout's claim before construction, so a pointer that would be read at the wrong offset is rejected rather than dereferenced.\n\n**Shared invocation context.** `_CPInvocation` holds what the four stages share for one call: device and stream binding, compile options, chunk geometry, and one alignment-checked pointer per `(address, dtype, alignment)`. Stages two through four reuse it. At the caller-visible boundary on a single `1x8192` two-head sequence, three processes: backend `0.883 \u2192 0.775 ms`, integration `1.053 \u2192 0.942 ms`, device time unchanged. The reduction is host-side.\n\n`_ptr_abi` is private and is not part of `chunk_gated_delta_rule`'s signature; the wrapper sets it for the SM8x branch.\n\n## Dispatch\n\n```python\nmax_seq_len >= 8192 and num_seqs * max(num_q_heads, num_v_heads) <= 8\n```\non compute capability 8.0, and the fused kernel otherwise.\n\nTwo restrictions:\n\n**An exact longest sequence is required.** `cu_seqlens` lives on the device, and reading it in the wrapper would synchronize on every call. `total_seq_len` over-states the maximum for every multi-sequence batch, which is where CP loses. `max_seqlen` may be any safe upper bound, so the SM8x rules read the exact maximum from `cu_seqlens_cpu`, the caller's host copy of `cu_seqlens`, through the same host-offset validation the Cake route uses. Without it, dispatch selects the fused path.\n\n**Compute capability 8.0 only.** SM86 and SM89 differ in SM count, L2 size and register file per SM, and neither threshold was fitted on them. They stay fused until measured.\n\nUnsupported checkpointing, state layouts or dtypes fall back to the fused kernel rather than erroring. An explicit `use_cp=True` that CP cannot serve still raises, because the caller named a path.\n\nMeasured through the public entry on ten cells, three processes each, at `c6ca8964` (`f026c462` changes comments and docstrings only): on the seven cells whose selection changed, what the wrapper now picks is 1.235x to 2.292x of what it picked before, at both boundaries, in every process. The three cells left on the fused kernel read 1.001x\u20131.006x, which is the same call measured twice.\n\n## The `v32` specialization\n\nOne cell was ahead on neither path: `1x8192` with 4 query heads and 16 value heads. CP declines it \u2014 `num_seqs * num_sab_heads` is 16 \u2014 and the fused kernel ran 0.911x\u20130.939x of Triton across the four boundaries below.\n\nAll V-dependent GEMMs in the fused kernel \u2014 the state update, `S@K`, new V, `O1`, `O2` \u2014 use `D_v` as the M dimension and split it across the warps. At 16 rows of M per warp, halving `D_v` leaves two warps idle without reducing per-warp work, so the dependency chain keeps its length. `moe_align_block_size_kernel` in `alphamoe_complete_small_alignment` (CUDA path) publishes `scan_buf` with a `__syncthreads()`. After it:\n1. threads with `tid < num_experts` write `prefix[tid] = scan_buf[tid]` (line 27359);\n2. every thread then binary-searches `prefix[]` to fill `expert_ids` (line 27372).\n\nThere is no barrier between the writes and the search. A thread can read `prefix[mid]` before thread `mid` has written it, and `prefix[0..num_experts-1]` holds no defined value before that write. This is a shared-memory data race, which is undefined behavior in CUDA C++. A stale read sends the binary search the wrong way, so a block of tokens can get the wrong expert id.\n\nWe tested SGLang's copy of this kernel, which matches this code around the race; we did not run this file. On an A100, Compute Sanitizer's `racecheck` reports read-after-write hazards between this write and the search, and under racecheck's thread schedule the kernel returned wrong `expert_ids` in 11 of 18 launches. With the added `__syncthreads()`, there are no hazards and the output is correct. At native speed we have not observed wrong output.\n\nThis PR adds `__syncthreads()` right after the `prefix[tid]` write. The new barrier sits directly below an existing unconditional `__syncthreads()` at the same scope, so every thread of the block reaches it. It costs one barrier per launch. Alternatively, the search could read `scan_buf[mid]`, which the preceding barrier already published and which holds the same values for `mid < num_experts`.\n\n## \ud83d\udd0d Related Issues\n\nThe same fix for SGLang's copy of this kernel: sgl-project/sglang#43030.\n\n## \ud83d\ude80 Pull Request Checklist\n\nThank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Philox draw reuse across consecutive speculative sampling calls.\r\n\r\n`get_seed_and_offset()` currently advances the generator and returns the advanced offset, so the current call starts beyond the range it just reserved. `chain_speculative_sampling()` also reserves `B * (N + 1)`, while rejection consumes `N + 2` draws per Philox stream: `N + 1` across the two acceptance loops, plus one recovery draw.\r\n\r\nFor `B=1, N=3`, consecutive calls currently start at offsets 4 and 8. A rejecting first call consumes offsets 4 through 8, reusing offset 8 in the next call.\r\n\r\nThis PR:\r\n\r\n- Returns the current offset before advancing the generator to the end of the current call's reservation. The no-delayer c128 row ran on a different node of the same type.\n- The trade-off is TTFT: prefill waits for the other ranks, and long prompts wait for alignment chunk by chunk.\n\nValidation on this upstream branch is still to be added.\n\n## Validation\n\n- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefill_delayer.py`: 14 passed (CPU). The tests cover each FIRE / HOLD rule and bound, the per-rank state, the scheduler gating and the config check.\n- `pytest -m cpu_test tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py` and `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py`: pass. They cover the changed `defer_prefills` expression with the delayer off.\n- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass, mypy included.\n- No GPU runs on this branch yet.\n\n## Details\n\n- **Protocol.** Once per engine step, each rank reports 6 ints in one CPU SUM all-reduce on the DP group: prefillable, pending prefill tokens (capped at `max_num_batched_tokens`), running decodes, KV usage >= 0.9, chunk in progress, prefill ran. Every rank then takes the same FIRE / HOLD decision for its next schedule.\n- **Placement.** The all-reduce sits next to `_has_global_unfinished_reqs()`. Every rank reaches that point on every non-idle step (real, dummy and pause steps alike), which the existing DP state sync already relies on, so the extra collective cannot be skipped by one rank. The state resets at each DP wave boundary.\n- **Rules (ATOM's), in order:**\n  1. A step that ran prefill arms `--dp-prefill-delayer-protected-steps` (default 10) steps that HOLD while decodes run.\n  2. FIRE if no rank has prefill, no rank decodes, or KV usage is high.\n  3. FIRE after 200 held steps, or after 100 with a chunk in progress.\n  4. HOLD until all ranks have prefill.\n  5. FIRE when the pending tokens reach 0.9 x prefillable ranks x `max_num_batched_tokens`, or when the backlog stops growing for 10 steps.\n- **HOLD scope.** HOLD defers all prefill compute, new requests and in-progress chunks, even on a rank without local decodes, so that ranks prefill together.\n- **Interaction with `--prefill-schedule-interval`.** The delayer replaces it; setting both is an error.\n- **Cost.** Off: none. On: one 6-int CPU all-reduce per step.\n- **Not supported:** elastic EP and custom scheduler classes.\n- **Relation to #51199** (cc @kjiang249). That PR coordinates releases through the DP coordinator (asynchronous, with acks and a 2-step lead); this one uses a synchronous per-step all-reduce in the engine loop and adds protected decode steps and a token fill target. We drove both decision functions in a CPU simulation of 8 lockstep ranks with agentic traffic:\n  - #51199's all-ranks release rarely triggered; most of its releases came from its capacity and 30-pass fail-open bounds.\n  - This delayer had 2-4x fewer mixed steps and about half the mean decode latency.\n  - #51199 had about 3x lower TTFT.\n\n  The two are complementary, and I am happy to merge efforts.\n\nAI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR.\n\n---\n\n<details>\n<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>\n\n- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. GPU util \u224887% at 220 W of 600 W \u2192 **communication-bound on PCIe**, not compute-bound. ~7K tok/s looks like the ceiling for this board without NVLink.\n\nRadix/prefix cache is the only large multiplier: cache-hit prefill **0.34 s for a 112K-token prefix \u2248 325K tok/s (\u224839\u00d7)**.\n\nDecode (client path over SSH tunnel, production config): prose 93.9 tok/s, structured/JSON 134.1 tok/s, TTFT 143\u2013169 ms.\n\n## DSPARK A/B (block_size=2, clean legs, each verified via `server_info` + acceptance length)\n\n| Prompt class | DSPARK ON | DSPARK OFF |\n|---|---|---|\n| prose | 76.5\u201378.9 tok/s | 36.4\u201336.5 tok/s |\n| structured | 120.3\u2013120.5 tok/s | 36.5 tok/s |\n| `accept len` | 3.0 tokens/step | 1.0 |\n\nWith DSPARK off the model flattens to ~36.5 tok/s regardless of prompt class \u2014 speculation is the difference between usable and unusable latency on this hardware. Production ships `block_size=6` (structured \u2248237\u2013252 tok/s vs 120 at block 2).\n\n## Traps that cost us experiments (SGLang-specific)\n\n1. **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a vLLM flag** \u2014 SGLang takes `ep_size`; the vLLM spelling is rejected outright.\n2. **`docker run` must pass `TP_SIZE`/`DP_SIZE`/`EP_SIZE` explicitly.** Without `-e`, the container silently serves TP8 defaults and your \"new\" config never happens (we recorded a full sweep of false data this way before adding a config gate).\n3. **`ep_size \u2264 tp_size`** or the MoE rank computation divides by zero: `moe_ep_rank = tp_rank % (tp_size // moe_dp_size) // (tp_size // moe_dp_size // ep_size)`.\n4. **DSPARK + DP attention requires `--enable-dp-lm-head`** \u2014 but is unreachable on this model anyway (next section).\n\n## Topologies SGLang rejects on this model\n\n| Attempt | Result |\n|---|---|\n| DP2 \u00d7 TP4 (any EP) | `ValueError: V4.1 vision currently supports TP/EP without DP, CP, PP or MoE A2A` \u2014 both replicas die within ~70 s |\n| prefill context-parallel | same class of rejection |\n| `--enable-dp-attention` alone | silently no DP group (`dp_size: 1`) \u2014 looks fine, isn't |\n\nOther SM120 gaps we hit: MSCCL++ (`_tune` kernel crash), FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, `flashmla_sparse_q8`, and CUDA-graph capture for **prefill** (crashes even with DSPARK off, i.e. unrelated to speculation).\n\n## Operational notes\n\n- A defunct container can survive a single `docker rm -f`; the next `docker run` then fails on the name conflict while an orphaned engine process keeps the port and answers health checks \u2014 which silently mislabels the next experiment. Balancing scheduling fairness and latency stability in such environments is critical; otherwise, severe head-of-line blocking and request starvation will degrade user experience. However, existing systems rely on rigid First-Come, First-Served (FCFS) policies and static token budgets, leading to fairness degradation and unpredictable latency jitter. To address these issues, we propose a fairness-aware and latency-controllable scheduling framework for chunked-prefill LLM engines. Specifically, we design a lightweight aging-based scheduling policy that dynamically calculates priorities using accumulated waiting time and remaining prefill work. Furthermore, we develop Latency-Prediction-Based Request Scheduling (LPRS) and Active Prefill Control (APC) to replace static budgets with target-time constraints and actively regulate prefill concurrency. We evaluated our scheduling framework on NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend accelerators using real-world workloads. Results show the aging policy reduces mean end-to-end latency by over 10\\% compared to FCFS. Moreover, LPRS and APC significantly reduce P99 tail latency and suppress prefill fragmentation, confirming that the structural prefill control and the temporal latency constraints are fundamentally complementary. For longer input prompt lengths,\nprefilling will incur a significant overhead on decoding time. In this work, we\nhighlight the following pitfall of prefilling: for batches containing\nhigh-varying prompt lengths, significant computation is wasted by the standard\npractice of padding sequences to the maximum length. As LLMs increasingly\nsupport longer context lengths, potentially up to 10 million tokens, variations\nin prompt lengths within a batch become more pronounced. To address this, we\npropose Prepacking, a simple yet effective method to optimize prefilling\ncomputation. In this paper, we study what happens during GUI grounding in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and identify a previously overlooked bottleneck. We show that grounding follows a two-stage paradigm: the prefill stage determines candidate UI elements, while the decoding stage subsequently refines the final coordinates. This asymmetry establishes prefill as the critical step, as errors in candidate selection cannot be effectively corrected during decoding. Based on this observation, we propose Re-Prefill, a training-free method that revisits inference by introducing an attention-guided second prefill stage to refine target selection. Specifically, visual tokens that consistently receive high attention from the query position, i.e., the final token, across layers are extracted as a preliminary target hypothesis and appended to the input, together with the instruction hidden states, enabling the model to deeply re-think its decision before coordinate generation. Experiments across four VLMs and five benchmarks, including ScreenSpot-Pro, ScreenSpot-V2, OSWorld-G, UI-Vision, and MMBench-GUI, demonstrate consistent improvements without additional training, with gains of up to 4.3% on ScreenSpot-Pro. On gfx950 that crashed every point with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` at the first prefix hit carrying a replay start. **gfx942 runs the same ROCm sparse path**, so this recipe pre-empts it rather than burning a sweep to rediscover it. Prefix caching stays on.\n\n## Memory\nWith the Engram tables offloaded, resident weights are ~81 GiB per rank at TP4, from the per-rank fit across the measured H100 TP8, H200 TP4 and B200 TP2 points (256 GiB sharded plus 17.2 GiB replicated). On a 256 GB card at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` that leaves roughly **100 GiB of KV per GPU** after the indexer's 32 GiB `[batched-tokens, 1M]` logits buffer. TP8 with the tables resident is unchanged at roughly 73 GiB per rank.\n\n## Test plan\n- [ ] `full-sweep-enabled` sweep: TP4 concurrency 1-32 AgentX + evals green\n- [ ] TP8 re-runs green on the new only on node caches. The new pin is the same upstream commit the MI355X arm moved to in #3326, on the plain ROCm channel that the gfx942 arms already use rather than the `rocm100` channel, which no gfx942 recipe has exercised.\n\nThat commit is also what makes this change possible: [vllm-project/vllm#57491](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57491) widened two `is_cuda()` gates to `is_cuda_alike()`, so `engram_config` finally resolves on gfx942. Bumping the image without setting it would silently move the TP8 tables to host memory and change that curve. Setting it explicitly to `false` at TP8 keeps the existing arm behaviourally identical, and `true` at TP4 is what makes TP4 fit.\n\n## Why `--no-swa-bounded-replay`\n[vllm-project/vllm#56227](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56227) turned SWA bounded replay on by default **between the two pins**. It relies on a window clamp that landed in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA kernels; the ROCm sparse SWA path only gained the `replay_start` kwarg. On gfx950 that crashed every point with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` at the first prefix hit carrying a replay start. **gfx942 runs the same ROCm sparse path**, so this recipe pre-empts it rather than burning a sweep to rediscover it. Prefix caching stays on.\n\n## Memory\nWith the Engram tables offloaded, resident weights are ~81 GiB per rank at TP4, from the per-rank fit across the measured H100 TP8, H200 TP4 and B200 TP2 points (256 GiB sharded plus 17.2 GiB replicated). On a 192 GB card at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` that leaves roughly **60 GiB of KV per GPU** after the indexer's 16 GiB `[batched-tokens, 1M]` logits buffer. TP8 with the tables resident is unchanged at roughly 73 GiB per rank.\n\n## Test plan\n- [ ] `full-sweep-enabled` sweep: TP4 concurrency 1-32 AgentX + evals green\n- [ ] TP8 re-runs green on the new -8.957845316329346}, {"id": "github:sgl-project/sglang:44030", "source": "github", "kind": "pr", "url": "https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44030", "title": "[Feat] hicache: Notify storage backends when the initial host-pool registration burst completes", "body": "## Motivation\n\nA storage backend learns its host pools from a burst of hooks: the anchor pool through `register_mem_pool_host`, then every pool of the host pool group through `register_mem_host_pool_v2` \u2014 but nothing told the backend when the burst was over. A backend that must finalize once the pool set is known (e.g. register the instance with a remote cache manager whose spec cannot be amended after registration) had no correct moment to act and could only defer that work to the first data-path call, paying seconds of setup on the first request and surfacing config errors (manager unreachable, instance conflict) after startup instead of failing it.\n\n## Modifications\n\n- `HiCacheStorage` gains a no-op `on_host_pools_registered()`: fires exactly once per attach, right after the last call of the initial burst; pools registered later (dynamic draft sidecars) arrive through v2 alone and do not re-fire it. Raising fails the attach.\n- The burst ends in different places on the two controllers, so each fires the hook at its own end: the base controller right after the anchor pool, `HybridCacheController` \u2014 whose per-pool v2 loop runs after `super().attach_storage_backend()` returns \u2014 after that loop. A `_registers_host_pools_after_super_attach` flag tells the two apart; no signatures change and no code moves.\n- The hook defaults to a no-op, so existing backends are unaffected.\n- Documents the registration lifecycle in `hicache_design.mdx`.\n\n## Accuracy Tests\n\nNot applicable (no model output changes).
